statement_en: Let $\epsilon,\delta>0$ and $n$ be sufficiently large in terms of $\epsilon$ and $\delta$. Let $G$ be a triangle-free graph on $n$ vertices with maximum degree $<n^{1/2-\epsilon}$. Can $G$ be made into a triangle-free graph with diameter $2$ by adding at most $\delta n^2$ edges?
statement_lean:
theorem erdos_82627 :
    ∀ (ε δ : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) (hδ : 0 < δ),
    ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ n ≥ N, ∀ (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj],
      G.CliqueFree 3 →
      (∀ v : Fin n, (G.degree v : ℝ) < Real.rpow (n : ℝ) ((1 : ℝ) / 2 - ε)) →
      ∃ (H : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (_ : DecidableRel H.Adj),
        G ≤ H ∧
        H.CliqueFree 3 ∧
        (∀ x y : Fin n, x ≠ y → H.Adj x y ∨ ∃ z, H.Adj x z ∧ H.Adj z y) ∧
        ((H.edgeFinset \ G.edgeFinset).card : ℝ) ≤ δ * (n : ℝ) ^ 2 := by
  sorry
